draft.title: Reading synoptic charts
card: A synoptic chart is a weather map. It shows air pressure at sea level using isobars, which are lines joining places of equal air pressure.
Isobars that are close together mean the pressure changes quickly over a short distance. This brings strong winds. Isobars that are far apart mean light winds.
High
marked H. A high-pressure system usually brings fine, clear weather.
Low
marked L. A low-pressure system, and the fronts linked to it, usually bring cloud and rain.
draft.remember: Close isobars mean strong winds. Highs bring fine weather. Lows and fronts bring rain.

a.q: On a synoptic chart, what does an isobar join?
a.why: An isobar joins places that have the same air pressure. Wind speed is shown by how close the isobars are, not by what each line joins, so it is the tempting wrong choice.
a.clue: The word isobar is about pressure.

b.q: On a synoptic chart, a town in Wagga Wagga lies under an H, with isobars far apart. What weather is most likely?
opts: Fine, clear skies and light winds
Fine, clear skies and strong winds
b.why: A high usually brings fine weather, and isobars far apart mean light winds. The option with fine weather and strong winds is tempting, but strong winds need isobars close together.
b.clue: Check what H means, then check the spacing of the isobars.

wants.brief: A simple synoptic chart of part of Australia with curved isobars, one labelled H and one labelled L. A cold front is drawn as a line with triangles. Isobars are close together near the L and far apart near the H.
wants.why: Seeing isobars, highs, lows and fronts together helps students read a real chart.

b.best: Fine, clear skies and light winds

problems.detail: The clue 'The word isobar is about pressure' gives the answer away, so students can pick the right option without knowing what an isobar is.
'A town in Wagga Wagga' is confusing because Wagga Wagga is itself a city. Use 'Wagga Wagga lies under an H' or 'a town near Wagga Wagga'.
The remember line says 'Highs bring fine weather. Lows and fronts bring rain.' without the card's 'usually', so it turns a general tendency into a rule.
